This tutorial walks a single dataset all the way through the *animovement*
ecosystem — from a raw [DeepLabCut](http://www.mackenziemathislab.org/deeplabcut)
export to a finished figure. It touches five packages, one per stage.

::: {.callout-note}
This is a **cross-package** tutorial. For details on any single function, follow
the links to that package's own reference site.
:::

## The workflow {#sec-workflow}

Each stage hands its output to the next, as shown in @fig-pipeline.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-pipeline
%%| fig-cap: "The five-stage animovement pipeline."
flowchart LR
  A["aniread<br/>read"] --> B["anicheck<br/>check"]
  B --> C["aniprocess<br/>process"]
  C --> D["animetric<br/>metrics"]
  D --> E["anivis<br/>plot"]
```

## 1. Read {#sec-read}

Point [`read_deeplabcut()`](https://animovement.dev/aniread) at your exported
file. Both the CSV and HDF5 exports are supported — pick the tab that matches
your file.

::: {.panel-tabset}
### CSV export

```r
library(animovement)

movement <- read_deeplabcut("path/to/DLC_output.csv")
```

### HDF5 export

```r
library(animovement)

movement <- read_deeplabcut("path/to/DLC_output.h5")
```
:::

The result is a tidy movement table — the shared data structure defined by
[anicore](https://animovement.dev/anicore) that every other package accepts.

## 2. Check {#sec-check}

Before processing, inspect data quality with
[anicheck](https://animovement.dev/anicheck):

```r
movement |>
  check_missing() |>
  check_pose_confidence(threshold = 0.6)
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Low-confidence keypoints
Pose-estimation exports often contain low-confidence points that read as valid
coordinates. Always check confidence before processing — otherwise outliers
propagate into every downstream metric.
:::

## 3. Process {#sec-process}

Drop low-confidence points and smooth the trajectory with
[aniprocess](https://animovement.dev/aniprocess):

```r
processed <- movement |>
  replace_low_confidence(threshold = 0.6) |>
  interpolate_gaps(max_gap = 5) |>
  smooth_median(window = 7)
```

## 4. Metrics {#sec-metrics}

Compute movement metrics with [animetric](https://animovement.dev/animetric):

```r
metrics <- processed |>
  calculate_speed() |>
  calculate_distance_travelled()
```

## 5. Plot {#sec-plot}

Finally, produce a publication-ready figure with
[anivis](https://animovement.dev/anivis):

```r
plot_trajectory(processed) +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Smoothed trajectory")
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Next steps
Swap `read_deeplabcut()` for another reader (`read_sleap()`,
`read_idtracker()`, …) to run the exact same pipeline on data from a different
tracking tool — see [aniread](https://animovement.dev/aniread).
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## A note on reproducibility
Code blocks above are shown for reference and are not executed at build time.
Once bundled example data is available, remove the display-only formatting so
the [scheduled validation build](https://github.com/animovement/animovement.github.io/actions)
re-executes this tutorial against the latest package versions and fails loudly
on any breaking API change.
:::
